principles: Preserve host-neutral experiment provenance rather than binding execution semantics to a single host.
Do not optimize or automate provider execution for its own sake; only document gates needed for correct Cell 03 execution.
Keep readiness evidence, execution evidence, and paper claims separate.
Use actual provider-reported usage after execution instead of pre-run dollar guesses as a correctness gate.
drivers: B-6529 readiness artifacts must not be rewritten into false execution evidence.
Cell 03 is the only permitted real-execution target for this story.
The user needs a status/ledger view showing done, in-progress, and remaining work.

options.name: extend-existing-m2-plan
pros: Keeps the execution path next to the frozen M2 readiness plan
Avoids duplicate protocol documents drifting apart
cons: The existing plan becomes longer and needs clear section boundaries

options.name: create-new-cell03-execution-document
pros: Could isolate execution details in a shorter document
cons: Reviewer already asked to avoid a standalone mega-document
Higher risk that B-6529 readiness state and B-991d execution state diverge

options.name: run-provider-calls-immediately
pros: Would produce data faster if everything else were already ready
cons: Bypasses result-row contract and B-991d provenance
Risks confusing probe logs with formal rows
Violates the current checklist and planning-only edit boundary

rationale: Extend the existing M2 provider execution plan first, because the immediate correctness issue is provenance and launch ordering, not running provider calls before the execution contract exists.

preMortem.scenario: Readiness evidence is mistaken for real provider results.
preMortem.trigger: The plan fails to distinguish B-6529 static launch readiness from B-991d execution provenance.
preMortem.consequence: Paper or lifecycle claims could overstate what has actually run.
preMortem.mitigation: Write an explicit B-6529 preserved-readiness and B-991d supersession boundary into the plan.

preMortem.scenario: Cell 06 or Phase 2 appears unlocked by Cell 03 readiness.
preMortem.trigger: The Cell 03 plan omits out-of-scope cells and claim boundaries.
preMortem.consequence: Later agents may run the wrong experiment order or overclaim evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: State that Cell 06, Cell 02, Cell 04, Phase 2, paper wording, product gates, and playbooks remain disabled.

preMortem.scenario: Cost accounting is blocked by a fake pre-run budget gate.
preMortem.trigger: The plan treats guessed dollar amounts as launch requirements.
preMortem.consequence: The experiment stalls on an unknowable estimate instead of recording actual usage.
preMortem.mitigation: Make pre-run dollar guesses non-gating and require postflight provider-reported usage/cost accounting.
